rows.name: PERFETTO_CONSUMER_SOCK_NAME

problems.code_says: The Tron column says Reads and sets, but the cell names only the reader. rinzler-capture.sh only reads the name. bin/ci/perfetto_capture.py sets it for the traced and perfetto processes that it starts and for the wrapped command. perfetto/test_perfetto.py sets it for a native traced and perfetto.

problems.statement: `rinzler-capture.sh` (the script that captures a Perfetto trace from a running rinzler) checks this socket before a capture. It stops when a program listens there. It removes an unused socket file that the user owns.
problems.code_says: The three sentences hold, but the cell describes only the read. It says nothing about the set: perfetto_capture.py builds the path consumer.sock inside a private socket directory and puts it into the environment of traced, perfetto and the wrapped command. The program name rinzler has no backticks.

cells.Where: `perfetto/tools/rinzler-capture.sh` reads it. `bin/ci/perfetto_capture.py` and the test `perfetto/test_perfetto.py` set it for the processes that they start.
cells.What Tron does with it: `rinzler-capture.sh` (the capture script for a running `rinzler`) stops when a program listens on this socket. It removes an unused socket file that the user owns. `bin/ci/perfetto_capture.py` sets a private socket path for its `traced` and `perfetto`.

evidence: perfetto/tools/rinzler-capture.sh:251 - the only read in the script: consumer_sock=${PERFETTO_CONSUMER_SOCK_NAME:-$default_consumer}; the script never assigns or exports the name

perfetto/tools/rinzler-capture.sh:248 - otherwise the default is /tmp/perfetto-consumer
perfetto/tools/rinzler-capture.sh:264 - the script ends with an error when a listener holds the socket
perfetto/tools/rinzler-capture.sh:266 - an unused socket file that the user owns is removed (rm at line 268); a file of another user ends the script (line 270)
bin/ci/perfetto_capture.py:125 - the consumer socket path is <socket directory>/consumer.sock
bin/ci/perfetto_capture.py:139 - _socket_env puts the path under the name PERFETTO_CONSUMER_SOCK_NAME
bin/ci/perfetto_capture.py:288 - the environment with both socket names goes to traced (line 305) and perfetto (line 326)

rows.name: TRACED_NOTIFY_FD

cells.Where: `perfetto/launcher-common` sets it for `traced`. The only reader in Tron is a fake `traced` that `perfetto/test_perfetto.py` writes.
cells.What Tron does with it: `perfetto/tronperf` and `perfetto/wrapper` start `traced` with file descriptor 3 connected to a named pipe. `traced` writes one byte to it when it is ready. The launcher script waits for that byte.

evidence: perfetto/launcher-common:304 - TRACED_NOTIFY_FD=3 "$TRACED" 3> "$daemon_ready_pipe" &: value 3, file descriptor 3 open on the named pipe
perfetto/launcher-common:299 - mkfifo creates the named pipe
perfetto/launcher-common:307 - wait_daemon_ready traced: the script waits for the byte
perfetto/launcher-common:264 - the wait reads the pipe with the time limit READY_TIMEOUT (TRON_PERFETTO_READY_TIMEOUT, line 14) and accepts only the byte 1
perfetto/tronperf:126 - tronperf calls start_perfetto_session
perfetto/wrapper:135 - wrapper calls start_perfetto_session
perfetto/test_perfetto.py:152 - the fake daemon script reads the name when it runs as traced; this is the only read in Tron
perfetto/test_perfetto.py:2582 - one test also sets the name for a native traced and reads the byte 1 from it

rows.name: GIT_TERMINAL_PROGRESS

cells.Defined by: Not known. The name starts with `GIT_`, the prefix of the git variables.
cells.Where: No reader in Tron. `CMakeLists.txt` sets it in the environment of the CMake configure step.
cells.What Tron does with it: The root `CMakeLists.txt` sets `1` in each configure run. It replaces a value from the caller.

evidence: CMakeLists.txt:68 - set(ENV{GIT_TERMINAL_PROGRESS} "1") at the top level, with no condition; set(ENV{...}) changes only the environment of the running cmake process and of the commands that it starts
git grep -w GIT_TERMINAL_PROGRESS - the only use in the checkout is CMakeLists.txt:68
git grep GIT_REPOSITORY - no CMake file of Tron declares a git download; the FetchContent declarations in CMakeLists.txt use URL and URL_HASH (for example CMakeLists.txt:277)
git log -S GIT_TERMINAL_PROGRESS -- CMakeLists.txt - commit 66b752ab79 (2024-04-26) added the line

outside the checkout: strings on /usr/bin/git and /usr/lib/git-core/git (git 2.34.1) and on /usr/bin/cmake (CMake 3.22.1) finds GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT and GIT_PROGRESS_DELAY but not GIT_TERMINAL_PROGRESS

unresolved: GIT_TERMINAL_PROGRESS - which software defines the name, and whether any program reads it. No code in the checkout reads it. The binaries of git 2.34.1 and CMake 3.22.1 on the audit server do not contain the string. A search of the current git source for the name (git grep GIT_TERMINAL_PROGRESS in git.git) would settle whether a newer git reads it.
notes: All 9 rows are in section 7, so no row has a For cell. PERFETTO_CONSUMER_SOCK_NAME is the only row with a factual gap: the Where cell and the last cell named only the reader, and now also name the setter bin/ci/perfetto_capture.py. The other 8 rows were factually correct and changed only for the house rules. (1) The 6 rows with Tron = Sets now start the Where cell with 'No reader in Tron.' in place of 'Nothing in Tron.'. Rows of section 7 outside this chunk still use 'Nothing in Tron.'. (2) TRACED_NOTIFY_FD and TRACED_PROBES_NOTIFY_FD: the definitions of traced and traced_probes were removed from the Where cells, as the glossary defines both. (3) DEBIAN_FRONTEND and INVOCATION_ID: the counts 'Two package test scripts' and 'One Dice test' were removed. (4) GIT_TERMINAL_PROGRESS: both sentences about the source comment were removed. The Defined by cell stays 'Not known.' and now gives the one checkable fact, the GIT_ prefix. The hint for this row proposed to keep the comment as a quote; that conflicts with house rule 6, so it was not applied. The other parts of that hint concern rows outside this chunk. (5) NO_COLOR: the variable name in the Defined by cell got backticks, and the cell now names the site of the convention. The first sentence of each cell names the two Perfetto scripts, so the reference is clear in context.
